source.section: PDF page 13, Line 13 Pensions (Employer-Funded Pension Plans, items (1) and (2)); Form N-11 line 13; Form N-11 lines 7-12, 19-20 and 23-27 (pages 2-3); PDF page 11 (Line 7), PDF page 20 (Line 23 standard deduction table, Line 25 exemptions), PDF page 9 (Lines 6a, 6b, 'age 65 or over as of January 1, 2026'), PDF page 20 (Line 27 Tax Table), PDF page 50 (2025 Tax Rate Schedules)

worked: Single, 70: a private employer's defined benefit pension 36,000 received upon retirement, to which the employee did not contribute (line 13 item (2)), excluded in full; interest 4,000, dividends 10,000. Age-65 exemption claimed. Line 7 federal AGI = private employer defined benefit pension 36,000.00 + interest 4,000.00 + dividends 10,000.00 = 50,000.00. Federal taxable income = 50,000.00 - 15,750.00 federal standard deduction - 1 x 2,000.00 age-65 addition = 32,250.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Line 11 total additions = 0.00; line 12 = 50,000.00 + 0.00 = 50,000.00. Line 13 pensions taxed federally but not taxed by Hawaii (private employer-funded plan, item (2)) 36,000.00. Line 19 total subtractions = 36,000.00; line 20 Hawaii AGI = 50,000.00 - 36,000.00 = 14,000.00. Line 23 standard deduction (single, PDF page 20 table) 4,400.00; line 24 = 14,000.00 - 4,400.00 = 9,600.00. Line 6e exemptions: 1 regular + 1 age 65 or over = 2; line 25 = 2 x 1,144.00 = 2,288.00. Line 26 taxable income = 9,600.00 - 2,288.00 = 7,312.00. Line 27 tax, Schedule I (PDF page 50) as bands on 7,312.00: 7,312.00 x 1.4% = 102.368; sum = 102.368, to the cent 102.37; tax = 102.37 (Form N-11 line 27 uses the Tax Table below 100,000 of taxable income (PDF page 20, Line 27): the table row 7,300 to 7,350 gives 103; this case uses the bands as numbers). No credits modelled (refundable food/excise and renters credits, lines 28-29, not claimed): state income tax = 102.37.
